title: Deepika Padukone Is Expecting Her Second Child. She's Also Shooting Fight Scenes for Two of Bollywood's Biggest Films.
excerpt: Atlee is deploying a body double for Raaka's action sequences while the actress returns to the King set 48 hours after announcing her pregnancy. Here's how two ₹300-crore productions are adapting.
body:
Deepika Padukone announced her second pregnancy with Ranveer Singh in April. The couple shared a photo of their daughter Dua holding a positive pregnancy test, and social media did what social media does — millions of congratulatory messages, a wall of heart emojis, and exactly zero consideration for what this means for two of the most expensive Hindi films currently in production.

The Math Problem

Deepika has approximately 50 days of shooting remaining for Raaka, Atlee's high-profile action drama starring Allu Arjun. The film's budget reportedly exceeds ₹300 crore. She is simultaneously committed to King, Siddharth Anand's Christmas 2026 tentpole with Shah Rukh Khan and his daughter Suhana, which carries its own enormous price tag and an immovable holiday release date.

Two films. Combined production value north of ₹600 crore. One leading lady who happens to be growing a human being.

Atlee's Plan B

According to Bollywood Hungama, director Atlee was "overjoyed" when he heard the news — and then immediately sat down with his creative team to figure out logistics. The solution: a body double will handle the majority of Deepika's action sequences in Raaka. The film features her opposite Allu Arjun in what's being described as an ambitious, genre-bending action spectacle, and the stunt work is substantial.

This isn't unusual in global filmmaking — body doubles and stunt coordinators have been standard practice in Hollywood for decades — but it's a relatively public acknowledgment for a Bollywood production of this scale. Atlee's willingness to restructure his shooting schedule rather than recast or delay signals both the actress's irreplaceability in the project and the industry's slow but real evolution in accommodating working mothers.

48 Hours

If anyone doubted Deepika's commitment, she answered it on April 21 — exactly 48 hours after the pregnancy announcement. She was back on the set of King at Golden Tobacco Studio in Vile Parle, Mumbai, filming a two-day action sequence. Trade sources describe the scene as a "highly stylised combat sequence" in which she and Shah Rukh Khan take on eight fighters simultaneously.

The timing is worth noting. She didn't take a week. She didn't send a note about needing to reassess. She showed up and did choreographed fight work.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs who grew up watching Deepika rise from the Om Shanti Om newcomer to one of the highest-paid actresses on the planet, this chapter is genuinely new territory. Bollywood's biggest female star is doing something that Bollywood has historically not known how to handle well: being visibly pregnant while remaining commercially indispensable.

The industry's playbook used to be simple — heroines disappeared during pregnancies, returned with a "comeback" film, and the machinery moved on. Kareena Kapoor shifted that narrative somewhat, but Deepika's situation is different in scale. She isn't attached to one film. She's the female lead of two concurrent mega-productions, and both teams are reorganizing around her rather than replacing her.

Ranveer's Parallel Universe

Meanwhile, Ranveer Singh has his own packed schedule. Coming off the combined ₹3,000 crore global haul of both Dhurandhar films, he's preparing for Pralay, a survival thriller directed by Jai Mehta (son of Hansal Mehta) set in a dystopian, zombie-outbreak Mumbai. The film will be co-produced by Ranveer and Hansal Mehta. Between the two of them, this power couple is currently responsible for what may be the most expensive combined filmography in active Bollywood production.

The Bottom Line

King is scheduled for Christmas 2026. Raaka doesn't have a confirmed release date yet but is expected to be one of 2027's biggest releases. Both films will feature Deepika in action-heavy roles. One will rely partly on a body double. The other apparently will not.

The industry is watching. If Deepika pulls this off — and nothing in her track record suggests she won't — it sets a new benchmark for how Bollywood's biggest productions handle their stars' personal milestones. Not as disruptions to be managed, but as realities to be worked around.

Baby number two is on the way. The fight choreography continues.
